findings.conclusion: Deferring budget-limited joint calls removes redundant failed full-graph searches without changing any constrained candidate journal or final route/authority on this cohort. Explicit no-growth rescue remains available and is independently tested. Counters are not latency or hardware speedup.

limitations: Single fixed 70-net development cohort; no held-out or full-design generalization.
No rescue transition was needed in this development cohort; rescue correctness evidence comes from explicit physical-graph fixtures, including successful and still-budget-limited rescue.
Deferral can change tree growth and later choices on other workloads. Equivalence is measured here, not a universal guarantee under a finite search budget.
The baseline equality is to the initial flat reroute, not the later hold-repaired tree. No fresh physical WL/CPD or DCP/STA/DRC signoff.
Still a serial centralized authority and source-observer shadow reference, not die-local concurrent ownership or a HBM accelerator.
next_work: Implement and verify a single authoritative owner partition per electrical resource, with stage-local access and explicit boundary communication instead of the current centralized authority/source-observer overlay.
Extend the same scheduling and cost protocol to representative held-out cohorts and full-design routing.
Complete physical QoR, HBM/die mapping and migration/topology ablations, accelerator synthesis/implementation, board performance/energy, paper and reproducible artifact acceptance.
